the far-infrared/radiowave and mid-infrared/radioweave correlations are universal, and that the scatter in these relationships is due to systematic variations in the infrared spectral energy distribution (IR SED) throughout the population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mid-IR and radio emission from star-forming galaxies is a robust indicator of the total infrared luminosity, even out to z = 1, where the rest-frame 1.4 and 70 μms wavelengths are shifted into the observed 24 and 4.9 μm bands.
the IR/radio correlation is not only valid out to z = 1, but that the correlation is also a function of wavelength.
the far-IR/radiation correlation holds out to z = 1 and that the mid-IR/1.4 GHz correlation is also valid to the same redshift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mid-IR and far-IR luminosities are both reliable tracers of star formation out to z = 1.
the far-IR/radiation correlation is valid to at least z ~ 2.
the IR/radio correlations are valid to z = 1 and beyond.
